reasoning:
I need to replace the arc-matching chain with an exchange rule, and add a put-down location rule for the released cube based on the nearest gripper coordinates at the reopen frame. Checking against earlier rounds, this stays consistent with the swap-by-swap requirement from round 2 and preserves the round 1 refresh behavior while now giving it a way to locate the cube.

Now I'm identifying the exact passages to replace: the chain description in both the annotator prompt and policy prompt sections, and the later-step logic describing how a held-then-released cube's position is determined versus the nearest listed cube fallback.

edits.modify_from: Then follow that cube as a chain through every remaining demonstration frame, one consecutive pair of frames at a time. In each pair, a cube whose position is within a few px of a position in the previous frame is the same cube; the cubes whose positions changed by more are in motion, and each one is matched to the new position that continues its own arc (closest to where its previous motion was heading), never to the position it started from. Carry the 'picked' label along with the cube it is on. Keep doing this through every frame until the last one, however many swaps occur and whatever partners they involve: a second swap commonly uses a different partner, so the picked cube can end two or more spots away from where it started; only two consecutive swaps of the same pair put it back. Do not decide by which cube is 'back' on the original pick spot: once any swap has touched that spot, the cube resting there afterwards is a different cube. Write the position of the labelled cube at the end of the chain, in the scene at the start of execution.
edits.modify_to: Then carry the 'picked' label through the shuffle one swap at a time. A swap is a run of frames in which exactly two listed positions leave their resting spots and, when the list is still again, the same two spots are filled again: the two movers have EXCHANGED spots. If the picked cube was one of the two movers, it is now on the OTHER mover's starting spot, never back on its own. If it was not a mover, it stays put. Do not use mid-crossing frames to decide where it lands; they only tell you a swap is happening. Repeat for every swap to the last demonstration frame, however many swaps occur and whatever partners they involve: two consecutive swaps of the same pair return it to its original spot; a swap of a different pair moves it elsewhere or leaves it alone, so it can end two or more spots from where it started. Do not decide by which cube is 'back' on the original pick spot: once any swap has touched that spot, the cube resting there afterwards is a different cube. Write the position of the labelled spot as listed in the scene at the start of execution.

edits.modify_from: if the execution steps shown contain a cube 'held in the gripper' that is then released (fingers reopen to 100% at height about 0.02), write that cube's position in the scene at this decision step; otherwise write the position of the listed cube within about 10 px of the carried value, or copy the carried value if none is listed. Ignore 'lifted off the table' lines.
edits.modify_to: if the execution steps shown include a frame where the gripper is at about height 0.02 with fingers partly closed and the fingers then reopen to about 100% at that height (a put-down), the released cube is the listed cube in the scene at this decision step that lies nearest the gripper's own [y, x] at that reopen frame: write that listed position. If it is absent from the list for a frame or two while the gripper rises over it, that is occlusion, not a sign that another listed cube is it; never locate it from 'held in the gripper' or 'lifted off the table' coordinates, which drift in mid-air. Otherwise write the position of the listed cube within about 10 px of the carried value, or copy the carried value if none is listed. Ignore 'lifted off the table' lines.
